2.note: a VALUE re-roll, not a shape one. All three read correctly at battle zoom and all three were dark enough to disappear against the plates they most often cross: cannonball on churned mud, shell and bullet on scorched and cracked ground. The cores repaint them mid-grey with a lit upper half and an edge line, so the silhouette survives on dark ground as well as light. A projectile is a few dozen pixels at field size and reads by silhouette and colour alone, which is why contrast against the plate is a correctness property here rather than a taste one.
